flashcards.back: A drawing that solves a word problem with bars: one bar for each amount, split into unit boxes, so the relationships in the problem can be seen before calculating.
One equal part of a bar: in the animation Mia has 2 unit boxes and Ben has 3, and every unit box is exactly the same length.
One whole bar split into parts: the class bar of 7 units splits into 3 units of boys and 4 units of girls.
Two bars for the same amount, before and after a change: Mia has 3 units before giving 1 away and 2 units after.
Drawn so lengths stand for amounts faithfully: two units is exactly twice one unit, never a guessed length.

The bar is treated as a rough sketch rather than a scale model. Every unit box must be exactly the same length: two units is exactly twice one unit. In the animation scene s4 the ruler proves Sam's units do not match, while the correct 2-unit bar is exactly twice the 1-unit bar.
